insight: legalClimbSpeedMult was added to stop rapid-climb tripping the height sentinel, but super-jump — shipped in the same PR — produces 11 consecutive illegal ticks and flags the player; a plain jump already sits at 4 of the K=5 threshold.
action: When adding an allowance to a validator for one new capability, enumerate every capability shipped in the same change set and add a test asserting the validator stays silent for each. Bound the height sentinel by the sim's own vertical envelope (max of climb rate and jumpSpeed*SUPER_JUMP_MULT), never by the climb rate alone.

insight: activePowerUps is an append-only array read with .find(), so a second orb of the same type creates two live entries; the HUD then emits duplicate React keys and shows the older orb's countdown. 62 same-type orb pairs within 3 floors occur across 40 run seeds.
action: When a collection is read with .find(x => x.type === t), enforce uniqueness by that key at every write site. On pickup, refresh the existing live entry's startTick instead of pushing a second one.

insight: The powerups.ts header states a 'one slot, a pickup replaces whatever is banked' design; the code stacks all five types simultaneously (2.625x combined climb/move) and powerups.test.ts:236 asserts stacking is correct. Doc, code and test disagree three ways.
action: When a module header states a balance or design rule, add a test that asserts the rule itself. If a test asserts the opposite of a header claim, treat it as a blocking contradiction and resolve it before merge rather than letting both land.

insight: Replacing the constant floorHeight = i * floorGap with a per-floor seeded RNG turned floorHeight and floorIndexAt into O(i) loops, making every per-tick geometry query O(floor^2): platformsNearY costs 0.07ms at floor 10 and 2.7ms at floor 1000, and the two affected test suites went from sub-250ms to 3.1s and 3.7s.
action: Before replacing an O(1) closed-form position formula with a per-index generator, add a prefix-sum or memo so cumulative queries stay O(1), and add a benchmark assertion at a deep index. Treat a >10x jump in suite runtime as a perf regression signal, not noise.

insight: orchestrator/tsconfig.json added exclude:[src/**/*.test.ts] in the same commit that added a CI typecheck job, and tsx --test strips types without checking them, so the four new test files are typechecked by nothing.
action: Never exclude test files from tsconfig to make typecheck pass. Add a separate tsconfig.test.json that includes them and run tsc against both configs in CI.

insight: retro.ts folds every open learning into '## Recently applied' and never promotes recurring lessons to '## Standing rules', never files them under '## By topic', and never trims the section to 20 — all three are promised by learning-loop.md:76-81 and CLAUDE.md. retro.test.ts asserts none of them.
action: Implement occurrence counting in foldLearnings so a lesson seen in 2+ iterations moves to Standing rules, trim Recently applied to 20 entries, and add a retro test per documented step. Until then, correct learning-loop.md and CLAUDE.md so they describe what the code does.

insight: loop/ is gitignored (.gitignore:5), so loop/learnings.md and loop/learnings.jsonl — described in CLAUDE.md as persistent cross-agent memory that is never deleted between runs — do not survive a fresh clone. This review had zero prior lessons available for exactly that reason.
action: Un-ignore loop/learnings.md and loop/learnings.jsonl while keeping loop/state.json and loop/handoffs/ ignored, and commit them. A memory the version control system deletes is not memory.

insight: The whole anti-cheat and replay surface (validateInput, isHeightDeltaLegal, newSentinel, updateSentinel, legalClimbSpeedMult, simulateFromInputs) has no non-test callers, so AC-11/AC-15/AC-16/AC-17 are asserted by unit tests against code no request path invokes. validateInput also zeroes climbY off-ladder, which would make ladder grabs impossible the moment it is wired in.
action: For any module claiming to be a security or anti-cheat seam, add an integration test that exercises it through the real entry point. If no entry point exists yet, record it in the handoff as unenforced rather than reporting the AC as covered.

insight: Refactoring checkout's branch-assigned locals from 'let blockId: string;' to 'let blockId = ""' silently disabled TypeScript definite-assignment checking, so a branch that forgets redirectSlug now yields success_url '/b/?payment=success' with no compile error.
action: Declare branch-assigned locals without an initializer so the compiler proves every path assigns them, or return an object from each branch. Never initialise to empty string or 0 purely to satisfy the declaration.

insight: hazard.ts survived four sequential retunes in one day and stayed coherent because the tuning constants carry the arithmetic in a comment and the tests assert the derived invariants (monotonic rise, closed-form equals numerical integral, mean speed above 1x). All three were independently verified and hold exactly.
action: For any tuned constant block that multiple commits will touch, write the derived invariant as a test (not just a comment) so later retunes cannot quietly break the guarantee the constants exist to uphold.

insight: REQUIRED_TEAM, REQUIRED_SEQUENCE, HANDOFF_STATUSES and PRIMARY_PIPELINE are the loop's enforcement mechanism but are exported as mutable Stage[], and teamMissing falls back to the shared REQUIRED_TEAM reference.
action: Declare any exported array that encodes a policy or invariant as readonly (or 'as const') so no consumer can mutate the rule at runtime.

insight: Full verification of the 2026-08-29 change set (77 files, 5081+/552-): 298 app tests across 19 files pass, 37 orchestrator tests pass, both tsc --noEmit runs clean. Slowest suites are powerups.test.ts at 3.16s and simulation.test.ts at 3.74s against a sub-250ms baseline for every other suite.
action: Track the powerups/simulation suite runtimes as a proxy for the towers.ts O(floor^2) regression; if they grow again, the geometry memo was not added.

insight: The anti-cheat module (validateInput, isHeightDeltaLegal, updateSentinel, legalClimbSpeedMult) is imported ONLY by test files. Every unit test passes, coverage looks healthy, and the production request path never calls it — so a security control can be extended for a new feature (power-ups) while providing zero protection.
evidence: app/src/game/antiCheat.ts:28,83,99,117 — non-test importers are only a barrel re-export in src/game/index.ts
action: For every security-control module, assert it is reachable from a request handler: grep the non-test importers before merging, and write at least one integration test that drives the control through the actual HTTP route rather than calling the pure function directly.

insight: A client-authoritative game simulation plus a self-reported score field plus a monotonic never-decreasing database write equals a permanently unrecoverable leaderboard. The monotonicity that makes the product invariant correct also makes poisoning irreversible.
action: Whenever a write is monotonic or otherwise irreversible, treat its input as a hard trust boundary: the value must be server-derived (re-simulated or recomputed), never client-supplied. If a route comment claims verification happens elsewhere, verify that path exists before merging.

insight: Stripe's checkout.session.completed fires with payment_status 'unpaid' for delayed-notification payment methods, and the enabled method set is Dashboard-controlled when payment_method_types is omitted — so whether the handler grants unpaid credit depends on config outside the repo.
action: In every Stripe webhook handler, gate the credit on session.payment_status === 'paid' and handle checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded separately. Never let a money-granting decision depend on Dashboard configuration that code review cannot see.

insight: This codebase has a correct constant-time token comparison helper in requireAdmin.ts, but the internal-token route hand-rolls a plain !== instead — the good pattern existed and was not reused. The same route is also the only sensitive endpoint with no rate limit.
action: Export constantTimeEqual from a shared lib and require every shared-secret comparison to use it. When adding any token-authenticated route, apply the same rate limiter used by the other privileged routes, fail-closed.

insight: Middleware forwards a shared secret to an origin derived from request.nextUrl.origin. It is safe today only because next.config.js leaves experimental.trustHostHeader unset; enabling that flag (a common fix when deploying behind a proxy) silently converts it into an unauthenticated secret-exfiltration primitive.
action: Never derive an outbound URL that carries a secret from any request-derived value. Build internal service URLs from an explicit env var (resolveBaseUrl / INTERNAL_BASE_URL).

insight: Replacing permissive defaults with explicit allow-list parsers removed a whole class of bug: the old code defaulted an unknown category to 'tech', letting client input steer money at a ghost season. The Aug 29 diff routed every money and view path through parsePaidStackSlug/parseSeasonSlug and switched dynamic lookups to Object.hasOwn.
action: Keep parsing untrusted identifiers through a single allow-list function that returns null on failure, and reject rather than substitute a default. Use Object.hasOwn for every dynamic property lookup keyed by user input.

insight: CI supplies STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, ADMIN_TOKEN and INTERNAL_TOKEN to a pull_request-triggered test job with no permissions block. Fork PRs are safe (GitHub withholds secrets), but any same-repo branch PR can exfiltrate them via a one-line test change, and install lifecycle scripts run in the same scope.
action: Use throwaway CI-only values for test secrets, gate secret-bearing jobs on github.event_name == 'push' or a reviewer-gated environment, add 'permissions: contents: read', and SHA-pin third-party actions.

insight: pnpm audit in app: 61 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 22 high, 30 moderate, 7 low), 24 unique high/critical advisories. next@14.0.4 alone accounts for 1 critical (CVE-2025-29927 middleware auth bypass) and 15 highs. yarn audit in orchestrator: 12 (3 high, 0 critical), all undici via @cursor/sdk.
evidence: app/package.json pins next to exact 14.0.4; pnpm audit --audit-level=high output
action: Bump next to >=15.5.21 (clears the critical and 15 of 22 highs) and vitest to >=3.2.6. Add 'pnpm audit --audit-level=high' as a CI gate so an exact-pinned framework cannot silently accumulate a critical CVE.

insight: The climb route comment states ranked results are re-simulated server-side from seed plus input log (AC-17) and that the path is separate — but no such route exists in app/app/api. The free leaderboard is nonetheless surfaced on the landing page next to paid stacks, so score integrity is already reputation- and revenue-adjacent even though it is labelled free.
action: Decide explicitly whether the free leaderboard is a trust boundary. If it is displayed alongside paid stacks, spec an AC requiring server-derived peak heights for it too, not only for ranked play.

insight: The climb renderer assigns canvas.width/height on every frame inside a state-keyed useEffect. Per the HTML spec, assigning the width attribute resizes and clears the bitmap even when the value is unchanged, so the full backing store is reallocated and zeroed 60 times a second. Raising useCanvasSize MAX_WIDTH from 560 to 2560 for fullscreen multiplied the cost to roughly 15MB per frame at dpr 2.
action: Only assign canvas.width/height when width, height or devicePixelRatio actually changed; clamp devicePixelRatio to 2 for large canvases; clear with clearRect on subsequent frames.

insight: floorHeight and floorIndexAt walk from floor 0 and allocate a fresh createRng closure plus a template string per floor, with no memoization. The renderer calls them six-plus times per frame, so per-frame cost grows linearly with altitude in an endless climber — roughly 1,700 RNG allocations per frame at floor 100 and 7,000 at floor 400.
action: Memoize floorGapForFloor and a prefix-sum of floorHeight per tower seed, and track the camera's floor index incrementally instead of re-deriving it from y each frame.

insight: Feedback hooks that hold previous-value refs across a game restart produce wrong cues: prevActiveKey retained a power-up from the previous run and fired a phantom 'X ended' sound and announcement at the start of the next run, and prevPickupTick collided with the reset tick counter and silently swallowed a real pickup cue.
action: Reset every previous-value ref in a feedback hook when the match seed changes or phase enters countdown; add a verifier test that plays two runs back to back and asserts no cue fires within the first 30 ticks of run two.

insight: A game key handler bound to window with an unconditional preventDefault breaks the surrounding page: Space no longer activates focused buttons in Chromium (Start climb, Climb again, the mute toggle) and the arrow keys no longer scroll to the how-to-play card. Adding a keyboard-operable button to a page that already has a global game key handler silently breaks that button.
action: Scope global game key listeners to the phases that consume input, and skip preventDefault when event.target is a button, link, or form control.

insight: app/ has no .eslintrc, so `pnpm lint` drops into the interactive next-lint setup prompt and lints nothing. In CI the Lint step printed that prompt and still reported success, so the gate passes unconditionally. Two eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps comments in the game loop suppress a rule that has never executed, and one makes a false stability claim about cfg.
action: Add eslint-config-next with react-hooks rules enabled and run `pnpm lint` in CI with a non-interactive flag that fails when unconfigured; treat any eslint-disable comment in a repo without a lint config as an unverified claim.

insight: Web Audio was created lazily from a React effect scheduled off a requestAnimationFrame setState, which is not a user-gesture context; WebKit requires resume() inside a gesture handler, so the first cue is likely silent on iOS. The mute toggle — the clearest audio-intent gesture available — deliberately no-ops when no context exists yet, so it does not unlock either.
action: Call ensureContext() synchronously from the Start button click handler and from the unmute toggle, and wrap every Web Audio node call in try/catch so an InvalidStateError cannot propagate out of a React effect and unmount the game.

insight: Three accessibility regressions rode in with the new HUD and controls: text-muted (#74707e) on void (#0a0a0c) measures 4.11:1 and fails AA for the 10-11px body copy in the HUD empty state and the lobby controls guide, even though ClimbCanvas.tsx already carries a comment rejecting that same colour for the same reason; the mute button is a ~28px target inside a strip whose fixed h-[46px] caps it below 44px; and an aria-live announcement built from a constant string does not re-announce when the same power-up is grabbed twice.
action: Reserve text-muted for decorative glyphs only and use text-secondary (8.1:1) for any body copy on void; give every touch-reachable control a 44x44 box before fixing a container height; append a monotonic counter to live-region text so repeated identical messages still fire.

insight: Passing the per-tick sim state through React state makes every consumer a 60fps component: usePowerUpFeedback re-runs a filter/map/sort/join useMemo and its effect every frame because the player object is cloned each tick, and PowerUpHud regenerates an inline linear-gradient style string every frame, forcing a style recalc and repaint alongside the canvas draw. The canvas itself draws in useEffect, which runs after paint, adding a frame of latency and a second composite.
action: Keep the authoritative sim state in a ref and draw the canvas from inside the rAF callback; publish to React state only at UI-relevant granularity (a ~10Hz tick for HUD countdowns, event-shaped values for feedback), never the raw per-tick state.

insight: A module-level Map cache with no eviction was safe while keyed by a stable per-category seed, but the switch to a fresh newRunSeed() per mount and per Start turned it into an unbounded leak: every run adds a permanent SpawnRec[] whose length grows with how high that run reached.
action: When changing a cache key from low to unbounded cardinality, add eviction in the same change; bound spawnScheduleCache with an LRU or clear it on run start.

insight: Removing a bad default value is not the same as fixing write-on-read. The ghost tech season 'fix' deleted every category='tech' default but left getOrCreateActiveSeason on three public read paths, one of which (the public record page) recreates the tech season specifically because parseSeasonSlug still accepts 'tech'. An anonymous visitor can now mint up to 75 ghost seasons instead of one.
action: When a bug is 'entity X gets created with the wrong key', grep the whole repo for the getOrCreate symbol rather than the file named in the report. Make read paths use the nullable getter and confine creation to authenticated write paths.

insight: readFileSync + expect(src).toContain(...) assertions give false green. Verified case: paidStacks.test.ts:21 asserts not.toContain('getOrCreateActiveSeason()') while the file calls getOrCreateActiveSeason(seasonSlug) — the empty-paren literal never appears, so the test passes while the bug it is named after is live.
action: Source-text assertions are acceptable only as a lint rule, never as proof of behaviour. Assert on invocation results with injected or mocked dependencies. If a grep assertion is unavoidable, match the bare identifier, never a call with specific parentheses.

insight: When a counter goes from global to per-partition, every Redis key that gates writes to it must gain the partition. views_k became per-stack but dedup:{session}:{bucket} and the hourly global ceiling did not, so a visitor browsing five stacks credits only the first; views_k now means 'sessions whose first stack visit this window happened to be here'. views_k is the sole input to burial and price-per-metre, so both are skewed across all 74 stacks.
action: Audit dedup, rate-limit and ceiling keys in the same change that partitions a counter, and add a test that credits two different partitions from one session and asserts both increment.

insight: In Next.js App Router the statically-optimized-but-should-be-dynamic bug class hits server component pages harder than route handlers. /climb awaits topFreeClimbers(50) but exports neither dynamic nor revalidate, so it is prerendered at build time and frozen forever; the .catch(() => []) fallback means a build without DB access bakes in a permanently empty leaderboard while the build still exits 0. All 12 route handlers are correctly dynamic.
evidence: app/app/climb/page.tsx:21; next build route table marks /climb as static; app/app/page.tsx:28 gets it right with revalidate = 60
action: Verify static-vs-dynamic by reading the next build route table for the Static vs Dynamic marker rather than reasoning about it, and never let a DB read in a server component fall back to empty data silently at build time.

insight: A partial or raw-SQL index that exists only in migration SQL and not in schema.prisma is invisible to the ORM and will be dropped by prisma db push or a regenerated migration. Here the P2002 race guard in getOrCreateActiveSeason and the rollover concurrency containment both rest entirely on an undeclared partial unique index, and the dashboard's user_id index is also undeclared.
action: Declare every index the application logic depends on in schema.prisma, and add an integration test that asserts the unique constraint actually fires.

insight: When a resource is partitioned, an unscoped aggregate endpoint cannot keep a single scalar state object in its response. /api/tower derives engine.ground, engine.rate, engine.growth and cost_of_rank1_usd from whichever block is rank 1 while each block's buried flag uses its own stack — the two disagree by construction, so a block can render above the ground line while flagged buried. The response shape is unchanged, so no contract test catches it.
action: Either scope the endpoint per partition or delete the now-meaningless aggregate fields. Never pick a representative member to stand in for a partitioned aggregate.

insight: In a Stripe webhook a 4xx means the provider never retries, so returning 400 for an unresolvable block permanently loses a captured payment. A 500 for a deterministic condition is equally bad: every retry fails identically until Stripe gives up. Both paths end in silent money loss with nothing beyond a console.error.
action: Any webhook branch that cannot settle must write a dead-letter row and alert, then return 200 so the provider stops retrying while the payment stays recoverable.

insight: Before hardening a module, check it has production consumers. The Object.hasOwn prototype-pollution fix was applied to app/src/lib/categoryUtils.ts, whose only importer is its own test — and that test asserts the six broad category slugs are valid while production gates on 74 subcategory slugs and 404s all six. The suite enforces the wrong taxonomy while looking green.
action: Grep for non-test importers before hardening a module. If there are none, delete the module and the tests that pin it rather than hardening dead code.

insight: Three unbounded findMany calls sit on hot paths: getRankedBlocks has no take and no select and is called with no argument from the public /api/tower (every visible block across all 74 stacks, s-maxage=3), credit-view then loops it with one awaited round-trip per above-ground block, and the webhook reads the whole stack just to findIndex one row. The scoped sibling route does it correctly with take:100 plus an explicit select.
action: Give every findMany a take and a select. Replace per-row awaited update loops with a single conditional UPDATE, and replace read-then-findIndex rank derivation with an indexed count.

insight: Season rollover is destructive and non-idempotent: every POST deactivates the active season and creates a replacement with views_k = 0, with no idempotency key, no check that ends_at has passed, and no dry-run, so a retried request rolls over twice and resets ground and pricing for the whole stack again. Concurrency is contained by the partial unique index but surfaces as a generic 500, so an operator cannot tell a benign conflict from a real fault.
action: Require an idempotency key and an ends_at-past precondition (overridable by an explicit force flag) on destructive admin endpoints, and return 409 with a distinct code for a uniqueness conflict.

insight: 185 assertions across 5 test files grep production source text with readFileSync+toContain instead of invoking behavior; 77 of 298 app tests (26%) never execute a line of production code, and no test anywhere invokes an API route handler despite 326 route lines changing on Aug 29.
evidence: app/tests/api/tower.test.ts (51 assertions, 16 tests, 100% grep); app/tests/api/checkout.test.ts:36; app/src/__tests__/v2.test.ts:54; app/tests/api/paidStacks.test.ts:25; app/tests/api/webhook.test.ts:19
action: Never assert an invariant by grepping source text. Invoke the unit and assert its output. Reject any test whose only failure mode is a rename.

insight: A not.toContain("fn()") assertion with empty parens is always vacuous: every real call passes an argument, so the literal never appears. Three such assertions pass while the bug they name is live.
evidence: app/tests/api/paidStacks.test.ts:21 vs app/app/b/[slug]/page.tsx:56; paidStacks.test.ts:42 vs credit-view/route.ts:63; paidStacks.test.ts:80 vs season-rollover/route.ts:33; the correct bare-identifier form is paidStacks.test.ts:30
action: Ban empty-paren string assertions. If a call must be absent, assert on the bare identifier, and prefer a behavioral test that the side effect never occurs.

insight: A test that re-implements production logic locally silently inverts as production evolves. v2.test.ts's copy of estimateDaysUntilBuried lacks the AC-23 null cap and uses Math.round with G0=10 while production uses Math.floor with DEFAULT_CONSTANTS (G0=0.65), so two tests now assert large positive day counts where production returns null.
evidence: app/src/__tests__/v2.test.ts:211-233 (copy, comment claims 'mirrors production exactly') vs app/app/api/dashboard/route.ts:44-60; failing assertions at v2.test.ts:242-246 and :259-267; G0*MAX_GROWTH=5.2 confirmed at app/src/engine/constants.ts:43,45
action: Never re-implement production logic in a test. Export the function and import it. If it is unexportable, that is the bug to fix first.

insight: A negative-lookahead regex in a not.toMatch guard exempted the exact dangerous form it existed to forbid: /altitude:\s*metresAdded(?!\s*\})/ does not match 'data: { altitude: metresAdded }', the non-additive overwrite ADR-7 prohibits. A duplicate assertion two files away lacks the lookahead and would catch it. Verified by executing both regexes against the dangerous string.
action: Prove every negative regex guard against a positive fixture of the string it must reject. When two files guard the same invariant at different strengths, delete the weaker one — it defines the real guarantee.

insight: The CI Lint step passes unconditionally without linting anything: app/ has no ESLint config, so 'next lint' prints its interactive setup prompt in a non-TTY and exits 0. Green for every commit on Aug 29.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:55-56; CI run 33252114342 Lint step logged '? How would you like to configure ESLint?' and reported success; no .eslintrc*/eslint.config.* under app/
action: Every quality gate must be proven to fail. Land a deliberately-violating fixture and confirm the gate goes red before trusting it; pass --max-warnings=0 and require a committed config.

insight: antiCheat.ts has no non-test callers (only a barrel re-export), yet 8 tests cite AC-15/AC-16/AC-18 as covered. simulation.ts implements its own divergent air-jump rule, and the two were measured disagreeing: validateInput returned rejected=true while stepMatch still granted the impulse.
evidence: app/src/game/antiCheat.ts; only referrer app/src/game/index.ts:12; simulation.ts imports powerups/hazard/towers but never antiCheat; rival rule at simulation.ts:301-310; tests at antiCheat.test.ts and powerups.test.ts:431-477
action: Before writing a test, grep for a non-test caller of the module under test. No production caller means the test proves nothing — wire it up or delete it, and never cite an AC as covered by a test of unreachable code.

insight: Same-type duplicate power-up pickup is untested for the four zero-cooldown types; the only duplicate tests use time-slow, the one type whose cooldown blocks the path. Measured: a second orb always collects, remainingTicks reports the stale first entry, and two double-jump orbs yield 4-5 mid-air jumps while doubleJumpChargesRemaining reports 2.
evidence: app/src/game/simulation.ts:416 unconditional push; app/src/game/powerups.ts:469 .find(); powerups.ts:518-522 consumeCharge decrements only the first entry; existing duplicate tests powerups.test.ts:250-278 and :510-522 both use time-slow
action: When a test covers the guarded instance of a branch, add the unguarded instances in the same commit. Enumerate the type/config matrix rather than testing one representative.

insight: Three load-bearing docblocks contradict the code they describe: powerups.ts claims a one-slot no-hoarding rule production does not implement (its endless-run balance argument rests on that false premise), tower/[category]/route.ts documents a six-value Category enum it now 404s, and learning-loop.md promises retro folding/promotion/trimming that retro.ts never implements.
evidence: app/src/game/powerups.ts:18-19 vs powerups.test.ts:236-248 and simulation.ts:416; app/app/api/tower/[category]/route.ts:7-9 vs :51-56; skills/closed-loop/learning-loop.md:79-80,98,109 vs orchestrator/src/retro.ts:126-133
action: When changing behavior, update the docblock in the same commit. Where a doc states an invariant, add a test asserting it — an untested documented invariant is a comment, not a contract.

insight: Two test files encode contradictory taxonomies and both pass: v2.test.ts asserts the six broad category slugs are valid via categoryUtils.ts (which has zero production consumers), while categories.test.ts asserts those same six are not valid stacks. Production gates on 74 subcategory slugs and 404s all six.
evidence: app/src/__tests__/v2.test.ts:198-203,288-305 vs app/tests/game/categories.test.ts:95-97; app/src/lib/categoryUtils.ts only imported by v2.test.ts; app/app/api/tower/[category]/route.ts:51-56
action: When a contract changes, grep the whole test tree for the old taxonomy and delete tests of the superseded surface. Treat a module whose only importer is a test as dead code to remove, not to cover.

insight: Tower geometry is O(floor) per query and O(N^2) per scan because floorGapForFloor constructs a fresh seeded RNG per floor: floorHeight scans cost 30.6ms/123.2ms/480.7ms for 400/800/1600 floors, and single queries cost 18.8ms/94.2ms at floors 1000/5000. No test would catch a further regression.
evidence: app/src/game/towers.ts:109-111,116-125,138-139; measured timings; no timing assertion in app/tests/**; no testTimeout in app/vitest.config.ts
action: Memoize the cumulative floor-height prefix and reuse one RNG per tower. Add a perf assertion on algorithmic shape (time at floor 4000 under 2.5x time at floor 2000), not a wall-clock ceiling.

insight: hazard.test.ts is the model behavioral suite in this repo: it sweeps monotonicity over 200s, feeds a hostile config (stumbleSpeedFrac:-1) to prove the lava still cannot descend, cross-checks against a closed-form integral with stumbling disabled, and pins the endless-run invariant to a named constant. 13 tests, 13ms, and every one can fail for a real reason.
evidence: app/tests/game/hazard.test.ts:108-115,141-149,151-167,128-139; contrast app/src/__tests__/v2.test.ts running 57 tests in 7ms because it touches nothing
action: Copy this shape for new modules: invariant sweep, hostile-config guard, closed-form or independent cross-check, and named-constant assertions instead of magic numbers.

insight: Five call sites invoke getOrCreateActiveSeason and only one is asserted against. An unauthenticated GET to /api/tower/<any of 74 slugs> creates a Season row, as does rendering /b/[slug] and the credit-view path — write-on-read, and an unauthenticated row-creation amplification vector.
evidence: app/app/api/tower/[category]/route.ts:59 (unauthenticated, untested); app/app/b/[slug]/page.tsx:56 (vacuously guarded); app/app/api/internal/credit-view/route.ts:61 (untested); guarded sibling app/app/api/tower/route.ts:6,30
action: Make getOrCreate* callable only from authenticated write paths; give read paths a read-only accessor returning null. Add a test asserting season.create is never called on any GET.

insight: Extracting a helper so scoping rules can be asserted without a DOM event, then only asserting the injected boolean, recreates the grep-test failure mode: the classifier (isInteractiveTarget / INTERACTIVE_SELECTOR) can rot while every test stays green.
action: When a DOM/policy classifier is split out for testability, the tests must construct the inputs the classifier actually sees (elements, events, payloads), not the boolean the caller already decided.

insight: A compatibility fallback that reads a field the simulation never writes is not a fallback. climb/result falls back to finishedTick for pre-ticks clients, but lava death only sets status=eliminated and leaves finishedTick null.
action: Before documenting old clients send field X, grep the sim for assignments to X. If the only write is the spawn initializer (null), either set the field at the event or do not claim compatibility.
